source_fields.formulation: A fixed unknown convex Lipschitz objective is defined on a Euclidean ball. Each round permits two simultaneous probes, each returning an independently Gaussian-noised value. Only the center incurs the true objective loss; independent noise does not cancel in finite differences.
source_fields.solution_goal: Minimize performance as defined by the metric, guarantee, and native resource.

source_fields.instance: The action center and both probes lie in the Euclidean ball $B_2^d(R)$. The fixed unknown objective $f$ is convex and $L$-Lipschitz on that ball, with normalization $f(0)=0$. Smoothness is not assumed.

structured_source_contract.objective: fixed unknown convex L-Lipschitz f on ball

source_fields.parameter_domain_description: L: $L>0$ (public); R: $R>0$ (public); T: $T\in\mathbb N,\ T\ge1$ (public); d: $d\in\mathbb N,\ d\ge1$ (public); \sigma: $\sigma\ge0$ (public)

operations.query_signature: $$Y_t^+=f(z_t^+)+\varepsilon_t^+,\qquad Y_t^-=f(z_t^-)+\varepsilon_t^-,\qquad \varepsilon_t^\pm\overset{\mathrm{i.i.d.}}\sim\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2).$$ The center $x_t$ and both probes $z_t^+,z_t^-$ must be submitted together before either observation is received. Noise is independent across all queries, with no shared seed. Only the center loss $f(x_t)$ is incurred; probe values are information queries and do not enter that round's loss. Causal policies may submit two simultaneous probes per round. Inputs $d,T,R,L,\sigma$ are public and $f$ is hidden. Both probes and the center must lie in the same ball. Past feedback may be stored and reused computationally; unrevealed past information and additional queries to exhausted samples are unavailable. Any within-round full-function or common-sample access must be explicit.

source_fields.feasibility: The output is the complete action trajectory satisfying feasibility and timing requirements. Randomized mixtures may be implemented before acting. Retrospective averages or convex combinations cannot replace actions that have already incurred loss. No additional optimal value or certificate is required.
source_fields.allowed_postprocessing: Previously executed online actions cannot be changed.
source_fields.certificate_requirement: No function value, optimality certificate, or final recommendation is required unless explicitly listed for this axis.

source_fields.base_expression: $$R_T=\sum_{t=1}^T\bigl(f(x_t)-\min_{x\in B_2^d(R)}f(x)\bigr).$$ Only the center $x_t$ incurs the true function loss each round. Noise realizations at the two probes do not enter regret.
source_fields.normalization: Use the cumulative quantity over T rounds without dividing by T. Preserve the displayed order of probability or expectation.
source_fields.finiteness_conditions: Two values within the ball differ by at most 2LR, so the absolute cumulative comparison is at most 2LRT. Observation noise is excluded from objective-loss differences.

$$N=2T\quad\text{independent scalar value evaluations}.$$ Exploration, initialization, and system identification all consume the stated online budget. Oracle calls, arithmetic, communication rounds and bits, and memory remain distinct coordinates of the resource vector; arithmetic and bit complexity are not certified as optimal.

source_fields.scalarization: Compare only at the specified joint budget and with the same native performance measure.
source_fields.setup_cost: All initialization, exploration, and identification calls are included in the budget.
source_fields.precision_model: Exact real-arithmetic model; bit complexity is unspecified

view_override_policy.limitations: Mechanical merge does not certify consistency or mathematical identity. Narrative qualifications and source conditions remain authoritative.

source_fields.randomization: Private randomness is allowed and independent of the fixed instance and future external randomness.
source_fields.adaptivity: Strictly follows the per-round and within-batch protocol of the oracle
restrictions: All measurable causal randomized algorithms obeying the stated information protocol are allowed. No linear-span, zero-support, or specific iteration restriction is added implicitly. Internal computation and memory are unrestricted except for the explicit computation, communication, or privacy constraints.

Private randomization is allowed, with the seed independent of the fixed instance and future external samples. Internal arithmetic, memory, linear spans, and iteration forms are unrestricted except for the stated computation, communication, privacy, and within-round interaction limits.
source_fields.internal_computation: Unrestricted except for explicit polynomial-time or protocol constraints
source_fields.parallelism: Follows the simultaneous-query, task-batch, and communication timing specified by the oracle

source_fields.complete_expression: $$\inf_{\mathcal A}\ \sup_{\substack{f\ \text{convex and }L\text{-Lipschitz}\\f(0)=0}}\ \mathbb E\!\left[\sum_{t=1}^{T}\left(f(x_t)-\min_{x\in B_2^d(R)}f(x)\right)\right].$$ Expectation covers policy randomness and all independent observation noise.
aggregation_order: Expectation covers policy randomness and all independent observation noise.
source_fields.quantifier_order: One admissible algorithm using only public information must handle every prescribed instance; adaptation to unknown budgets must be performed by that same algorithm.
randomness_sources: Observation or environment randomness explicitly allowed by the oracle.
source_fields.runtime_guarantee: The resource budget is fixed. Expected error is not automatically converted to high probability or a random-runtime bound.

source_fields.precision_model: Exact real-arithmetic model; bit complexity is unspecified
